issues.note: Backend (decentraland/metamorph), not client: the explorer does not decode GIFs; NFT GIFs are detected as video through the metamorph converter (LoadNFTTypeSystem HEAD on /convert -> video/*) and played by the media player as an MP4. metamorph ConverterService.ConvertFrames coalesces the GIF frames with ImageMagick and passes them to ffmpeg's concat input with no per-frame duration, so ffmpeg uses its 25 fps default and drops the GIF delays. 600 frames / 25 fps = 24 s, which matches QA's 24.1 s. The fix belongs in metamorph: write a concat list with each frame's AnimationDelay as its duration, or let ffmpeg read the GIF directly. Separate client observation: since #7780 the NftTypeResult URL is the raw image_url, so the video player opens the original URL rather than the converted MP4; worth a check by the media owners, but it does not change the frame timing.

Separate from #8721 (that one is a duplicate report; this is post-failure state recovery). The same-realm path (RealmNavigator.TeleportToParcelAsync -> MoveToParcelInSameRealmTeleportOperation) has no rollback: while pending, CheckCameraQualifiedForRepartitioningSystem points scene partitioning at the destination (source scene unloads) and TeleportCharacterSystem pins the avatar at the destination, and on timeout it only removes the intent. Restoring the source would need a rollback across RealmNavigator, partitioning and scene readiness (keep the source until commit, or re-teleport after failure), which is not a minimal local fix. The reported state (avatar still at 100,100) also contradicts that code path, and the issue says the cause of the timeout is unknown, so the failing stage needs the instrumented repro the issue asks for.

Engine-internal FMOD log with no managed frames (FMOD_ERR_CHANNEL_STOLEN): Unity polls a voice that FMOD stole because the 512 virtual-voice pool (ProjectSettings/AudioManager m_VirtualVoiceCount) ran out. Sentry R5J: 1 user, 1123 events over 11h at the 1/s debounce rate, with no scene tag and only a 404 media-stream retry in the breadcrumbs. Earlier occurrences #7707 and #10361 were never fixed (Sentry auto-resolved one; the other was closed as a duplicate). Voice exhaustion means audio actually drops, and it could be scene content or a client AudioSource leak, so a gateway filter would hide a possibly real defect. Needs a repro with an audio voice count to tell which.
